title: Optimizers: SGD, Momentum and Adam
overview: Optimizers decide how gradients become parameter updates. Momentum and adaptive methods like Adam speed up and stabilize training compared with plain SGD.
objectives: Explain Adam's moment estimates and bias correction
Use learning rate schedules and warmup

method.title: Gradient descent
method.body: Updates follow w -= lr * g; mini-batches give a noisy but cheap gradient estimate.

method.title: Momentum
method.body: A velocity term accumulates past gradients, damping oscillations and speeding progress along consistent directions.

method.title: Adam
method.body: Tracks running means of the gradient and squared gradient, giving each parameter its own step size.

method.title: Schedules
method.body: Warmup, cosine decay or step decay of the learning rate often matter as much as the optimizer choice.

pseudocode:
m = b1*m + (1-b1)*g
v = b2*v + (1-b2)*g*g
m_hat = m / (1 - b1**t)
v_hat = v / (1 - b2**t)
w -= lr * m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
def grad(w): return 2 * (w - np.array([3.0, -2.0]))  # minimize ||w - target||^2
w = np.zeros(2); m = np.zeros(2); v = np.zeros(2)
lr, b1, b2, eps = 0.1, 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
for t in range(1, 201):
    g = grad(w)
    m = b1 * m + (1 - b1) * g
    v = b2 * v + (1 - b2) * g * g
    w -= lr * (m / (1 - b1 ** t)) / (np.sqrt(v / (1 - b2 ** t)) + eps)
print("Adam solution:", np.round(w, 3))
